title: Product rule for independent word events
statement: Let $m_1,m_2\in\mathbb N$, and let $A$ and $B$ be predicates on Boolean words. For a uniformly random Boolean word of length $m_1+m_2$, the probability that its first $m_1$ bits satisfy $A$ and its remaining $m_2$ bits satisfy $B$ equals the product of the probability that a uniformly random length-$m_1$ word satisfies $A$ and the probability that a uniformly random length-$m_2$ word satisfies $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ and $B$ are predicates on Boolean words
